subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should every non-ClawHub plugin install and repair path fail closed unless it receives this explicit source-provenance acknowledgement?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but deciding whether existing automation must immediately add a new flag is a security, compatibility, and rollout-policy choice that cannot be inferred from tests alone.

options.title: Approve the fail-closed gate
options.body: Require explicit acknowledgement across direct installs, updates, setup, doctor, and repair paths, with upgrade documentation and exact-head proof.

options.title: Narrow the mandatory gate
options.body: Require acknowledgement on direct installer surfaces while temporarily preserving selected established setup or repair workflows.

options.title: Pause the rollout
options.body: Keep current behavior until ClawHub trust metadata and the operator upgrade path are fully deployed.

recommendation.title: Approve the fail-closed gate
recommendation.body: Require explicit acknowledgement across direct installs, updates, setup, doctor, and repair paths, with upgrade documentation and exact-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the strongest merged feature history for both the existing ClawHub trust boundary and this follow-up policy.
